## Personality

Eliza Andrews is characterized by an exceptionally grim demeanor and a deeply ingrained pessimistic outlook. She is widely regarded as a born pessimist who holds no hope for the future, serving as a benchmark for gloominess to those around her.

_Sources: [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P14](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0014), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P60](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0060), [v2 VIII Marilla Adopts Twins P24](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0024), [v2 XVII A Chapter of Accidents P64](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0064)_

## History

Eliza Andrews was born a pessimist and lived in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) alongside her optimistic sister, Catherine. During a visit from [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md), who were canvassing the neighborhood to collect subscriptions for repairs to the local hall on behalf of the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvers), the sisters were encountered by the two girls.

_Sources: [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P2](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0002), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P6](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0006), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P11](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0011), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P13](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0013), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P14](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0014), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P17](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0017), +154 more_

## Quotes

> "I don’t see the necessity. We didn’t gad about to halls and places when we were young, Catherine Andrews. This world is getting worse every day."
>
> — Eliza Andrews — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P18](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0018)

> "Doctors always talk like that just to keep people cheered up. I wouldn’t have much hope if I was her. It’s best to be prepared for the worst."
>
> — Eliza Andrews — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P27](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0027)

> “You think!” Miss Eliza’s voice expressed the utmost contempt. “It doesn’t signify what you think, Catherine Andrews. Facts is facts.”
>
> — Eliza Andrews — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P20](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0020)

> "There isn’t any bright side."
>
> — Eliza Andrews — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P22](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0022)
